title: Meta Stock Falls 5.9% as AI Stocks Slide (Nov 20)
summary: META fell 5.93% to $560.84 on Nov 20 as an AI stock selloff pulled the Nasdaq down 5.28%. See how Meta traded and what drove the drop.
body_markdown:
## Why Meta Stock Fell


None of the coverage cited here named a Meta-specific cause for Friday's decline; financial media tied the drop to a broad selloff in AI stocks. According to CNBC's live market coverage, the closely watched[Anthropic IPO](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/anthropic-ipo-prices-83-raises-81-billion/) led investors to take profits on the AI-led rally rather than revive it, and Anthropic's Friday decline gave back much of its debut gain, pressuring the broader AI trade.


CNBC also reported, citing Reuters, that the US Securities and Exchange Commission is exploring possible accounting issues at Nvidia. As reported by[The Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stock-market-today-nov-20-223513707.html) , Nvidia fell following reports of a potential SEC accounting probe that accelerated a broader unwind of artificial intelligence trades, while Broadcom fell on unconfirmed reports that Google would cut next year's chip shipments.


With no company news cited, Meta tracked the market: slightly deeper than the Nasdaq, deeper than other large platform names and far shallower than the chipmakers at the center of the selloff.


## META Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Meta's ad revenue rose 25.9% year over year to $63.1 billion in the third quarter of 2026, with the average price per ad up 14% and impressions up 10%, according to[The Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/mark-zuckerberg-meta-platforms-pouring-043101493.html) .
- The same report put daily active users across Meta's family of apps at 3.64 billion.
- Meta CFO Susan Li, as quoted by The Motley Fool, said the company is "leveraging AI to make it easier for businesses to manage campaigns, develop creative, and act on performance opportunities."


### Risks


- According to The Motley Fool, Meta will invest up to $145 billion in capital expenditures in 2026, with spending likely to be much higher next year, which has turned[free cash flow](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/free-cash-flow-and-net-cash-flow-explained-2/) negative and led to a pause in share buybacks.
- Advertising made up 98% of total revenue in the third quarter of 2026, and the same report described Meta's newer AI revenue lines as immaterial for now.
- Sector sentiment remains fragile: Friday's selloff was driven by reports around Nvidia and Broadcom, some of them unconfirmed, and AI-linked stocks moved together.
